newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to chair national dialogue, Hamas boycotts.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to chair national dialogue, Hamas boycotts.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and opponents of his deadlocked peace accords with Israel will meet on Monday to search for "common ground", PLO officials said.

But members of the militant Islamic movement Hamas in the West Bank and Gaza Strip said they would boycott the national unity talks set to start late on Monday in the West Bank city of Nablus because Arafat had yet to free some of the movement's activists.
Hamas, opposed to Palestinian-Israeli peace deals, has claimed responsibility for several suicide bombings in Israel that killed scores of people and wounded dozens.
"We will try to find a way to reach common ground to face Israel's refusal to implement peace deals," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general-secretary of the presidency.

Unlike a previous meeting in February, Arafat is expected to face sharp criticism over security links with Israel in light of its Jewish settlement activity which sparked street protests and led to a halt in peace talks.
Arafat said on Sunday Israeli and Palestinian security officials had met to discuss the stabbing death of two Israeli women whose bodies were found on Friday in a West Bank nature reserve.

Seven Palestinians have been killed in clashes with Israeli troops since Israel broke ground on March 18 to build a new Jewish settlement at a hilltop in Arab East Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
On March 21 a Moslem militant set off a bomb in a Tel Aviv cafe killing three Israeli women and himself.

"After four years we have reached the conclusion that the PLO-Israeli peace deals are a failure so we believe the dialogue should be aimed at finding other alternatives," said Abdel-Rahim Mallouh, member of the Politburo of the radical Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

Hamas participated in the first national unity dialogue held last February 27 hoping to improve relations with the Palestinian Authority. The militant Islamic Jihad has stayed away from both meetings.

"Hamas has decided to boycott this meeting because it has not been properly prepared for and the Authority has not made goodwill gestures by releasing jailed members of the movement," said Hamas official Jamal Mansour.
